review_candidates.description: Position: Director of Operations (Supply Chain & Logistics) | Buffalo Bicycles Location: Kenya, Malawi, Tanzania, Uganda, or Zambia Reporting to: Executive Director of Partnerships and Country Strategy About Us World Bicycle Relief mobilizes communities in rural regions around the world to thrive with life-changing bicycles. We partner with communities to expand access to education, markets, healthcare, and other essential services. With our purpose-designed Buffalo Bicycles, individuals in low-income regions are a force for change, unlocking pathways to new opportunities for themselves, their families, and entire communities. We are a mission-driven, global nonprofit social enterprise that manages a bicycle supply chain from design through final distribution. Through World Bicycle Relief, we provide transportation solutions to those who cannot afford them, while Buffalo Bicycle Ltd. sells bicycles and spare parts and supports repair and maintenance services through local shops and mechanics. Purpose of the Position World Bicycle Relief is seeking an experienced Director of Operations (Supply Chain & Logistics) to lead and strengthen the global operations of Buffalo Bicycles, ensuring bicycles, components, and spare parts are sourced, assembled, and distributed efficiently, reliably, and cost-effectively. Reporting to the Executive Director of Partnerships and Country Strategy, this role provides global leadership across supply chain, procurement, logistics, inventory management, warehousing, assembly operations, quality assurance, and distribution. The Director will work closely with country leadership and cross-functional teams to establish consistent operational standards, strengthen systems and processes, improve performance, and support growth across existing and new markets. While country teams maintain responsibility for local execution, the Director provides technical expertise, strategic guidance, and operational support across geographies. The ideal candidate brings strong international supply chain and assembly operations experience, analytical problem-solving skills, and the ability to build collaborative relationships across diverse teams and markets. Job Responsibilities Supply Chain, Procurement, and Logistics Lead and improve Buffalo Bicycles' global supply chain, including supplier coordination, procurement, international freight, customs, transportation, and distribution. Develop scalable supply and logistics plans aligned with demand forecasts, production capacity, and organizational growth. Strengthen supplier performance, cost efficiency, risk management, and coordination with country teams and Product Development. Inventory, Warehousing, and Distribution Establish consistent global standards for inventory management, warehousing, and distribution. Improve inventory planning, stock visibility, accuracy, and traceability across suppliers, warehouses, assembly facilities, and markets. Partner with country Operations teams to strengthen inventory controls, minimize stockouts and excess inventory, and ensure reliable product availability and fulfillment. Assembly Operations and Quality Provide global technical leadership and support for bicycle assembly operations, ensuring consistent standards for safety, efficiency, quality, and productivity. Partner with Product Development and country teams to improve assembly processes, production planning, quality controls, and technical troubleshooting. Identify opportunities to strengthen assembly capacity, reduce waste, and improve operational performance. Operations Strategy, Planning, and Growth Develop and implement a global Operations strategy aligned with Buffalo Bicycles' organizational priorities and growth objectives. Translate sales forecasts, partnership commitments, and market needs into coordinated supply, inventory, assembly, and logistics plans. Support operational planning for new markets, partnerships, and products while collaborating with Finance on budgets, costs, and working capital requirements. Operational Performance and Continuous Improvement Establish global operational performance measures and reporting practices across supply chain, inventory, logistics, assembly, quality, and fulfillment. Use data and operational insights to identify inefficiencies, improve productivity, reduce costs, and strengthen decision-making. Promote continuous improvement, shared learning, and capability building across country Operations teams. Leadership and Culture Expectations The Director of Operations will model and strengthen World Bicycle Relief's values by: Building trusted partnerships across countries, functions, and cultures. Providing technical leadership, coaching, and support while respecting local ownership and accountability. Demonstrating integrity, sound judgment, and responsible stewardship of organizational resources. Promoting continuous improvement, collaboration, and operational excellence. Strengthening accountability, transparency, and knowledge sharing across teams. Requirements Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Engineering, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Substantial progressively responsible experience in operations, supply chain, logistics, manufacturing, assembly, or related disciplines, including leadership experience. Demonstrated experience managing complex international supply chains, including procurement, freight, customs, warehousing, inventory, and distribution. Strong experience with manufacturing or assembly operations, production planning, quality management, and continuous improvement. Experience in demand forecasting, inventory planning, supplier management, and operational performance analysis. Strong financial and commercial understanding, including operating budgets, inventory costs, landed costs, and working capital. Experience using ERP, inventory management, procurement, logistics, or supply chain planning systems. Demonstrated ability to establish operational standards and influence geographically dispersed teams. Strong analytical, problem-solving, project management, and communication skills. Preferred Experience working across multiple countries and cultures, particularly in African markets. Advanced degree or relevant professional certification in supply chain, operations, or a related field. Experience supporting operational expansion into new markets. Experience in a social enterprise, international nonprofit, or mission-driven commercial organization. Working Conditions This is a global role requiring regular collaboration across multiple countries and time zones, as well as periodic international travel to suppliers, assembly facilities, warehouses, and Buffalo Bicycle operating markets. We recognize that strong candidates may not meet every qualification listed. If you have significant experience in operations, supply chain, logistics, or assembly and are excited about our mission, we encourage you to apply. WBR is a registered not-for profit in the USA (501c3), Canada, UK, Germany, Switzerland, and Australia. We have supported programs in 20 countries, and have country offices, staff, and assembly facilities in Colombia, Kenya, Malawi, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia. WBR is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

review_candidates.title: Database Change and Delivery Lead - Remote / Work from Home
review_candidates.description: The Australia Institute is one of Australia’s leading independent think tanks, conducting research and advocacy on economic, social, environmental and political issues. Our work is grounded in economic fairness, democratic accountability, environmental sustainability and evidence-based public policy. We are seeking a Database Change and Delivery Lead to manage the end-to-end delivery of a migration program. The role coordinates technical work with internal teams and external partners, and makes sure staff are ready, confident and supported to work in the new system from day one. This is a delivery and engagement role first. You will not be expected to write the migration code yourself, but you must understand database migration well enough to plan it realistically, challenge assumptions, manage the process and spot risk early. Key responsibilities Program and change delivery Plan, schedule and lead delivery of the database migration program, including scope, milestones, dependencies, resourcing and budget tracking. Apply a structured change and project methodology. Coordinate the migration lifecycle: current-state discovery, data mapping, cleansing and de-duplication, test loads, user acceptance testing, cutover and post-go-live stabilisation. Maintain the program's risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies log and escalate early with clear options. Manage external vendors, implementation partners and contractors against agreed deliverables, timeframes and cost. Define and run go/no-go criteria, cutover runbooks, rollback plans and hypercare arrangements. Stakeholder engagement and change management Identify and map stakeholders, and build a tailored engagement and communications plan for each group. Act as the main point of contact between leadership, end users, data and IT staff, and external partners. Run workshops to capture business requirements, current processes and future-state design decisions. Lead change impact assessments and plan training, guides and support so staff can adopt the new system. Develop and deliver practical staff training, providing hands-on guidance, ongoing support and troubleshooting throughout the transition to Salesforce, ensuring staff are confident and capable of using the new system effectively. Build and support a network of internal champions or super-users. Provide regular, plain-English status reporting to the executive and any steering committee. Data governance and quality Work with data owners to agree data migration rules, retention decisions and acceptance criteria. Make sure the migration complies with privacy obligations, including the Privacy Act 1988 and the Australian Privacy Principles, and any consent and fundraising requirements. Oversee reconciliation and validation so migrated records are complete, accurate and auditable. Document decisions, data dictionaries and new processes so knowledge stays with the organisation after the program ends. Selection criteria Essential Proven experience leading or delivering at least one end-to-end database or CRM migration program, from discovery through cutover and post-go-live support. Demonstrated project and change delivery experience, including planning, scheduling, risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies log management, budget tracking and status reporting. Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with a track record of building trust across executive, operational and technical audiences. Practical understanding of data migration concepts: data mapping, transformation, cleansing, de-duplication, test loads, reconciliation and cutover planning. Experience managing vendors or implementation partners against contracted deliverables. Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical risk in plain English. Ability to work independently in a part-time, hybrid arrangement and prioritise effectively across competing demands. Desirable Hands-on experience with Salesforce migrations or implementations, ideally Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, NPSP or a similar CRM data model. Familiarity with migration and integration tools such as Salesforce Data Loader, Data Import Wizard, dataloader.io, MuleSoft or SQL-based ETL. Experience in the not-for-profit, research, policy or advocacy sectors, including supporter, donor or membership data. Experience with reporting tools such as Power BI or Salesforce reports and dashboards. Working arrangements and how to apply 3 days per week. Work is remote or from our Canberra office, with on-site days in Canberra required around workshops, UAT and cutover. Occasional flexibility outside core hours may be needed during cutover windows. To apply as soon as possible: A current CV (doc. or pdf.) A cover letter of no more than two pages (doc. or pdf.) A short summary of one database migration program you delivered (doc. or pdf.) For a confidential discussion about the role, contact Ian Coleman, Fundraising Director, ian.coleman@australiainstitute.org.au using the subject line: Database Change and Delivery Lead - Remote / Work from Home enquiry via EthicalJobs or 0408 274 781.

review_candidates.description: 该职位来源于猎聘 核心职责 1、需求对接：与业务部门沟通，将数据需求转化为BI报表及分析方案的技术规格。 2、报表开发：使用Tableau/Power BI等工具设计开发交互式仪表盘、标准化报表及自助分析模型。 3、数据建模：参与数据仓库分析层模型设计，编写高效SQL进行多源数据提取与整合。 4、洞察分析：深度挖掘数据趋势与异常，产出分析报告，通过数据叙事支持战略决策。 5、用户支持：培训业务人员使用BI工具，推广自助分析，收集反馈改进产品。 6、质量保障：监控关键指标，维护数据定义与标准，确保数据一致性。 任职要求 1、学历：本科及以上，数学/统计/运筹学等相关专业。 2、经验：3年以上BI或数据分析全职经验。 3、技能：精通SQL（含复杂查询及调优）；精通至少一种BI工具（如Tableau、Power BI）；熟悉数据仓库建模及ETL。 4、素质：出色的业务理解与逻辑分析能力，优秀沟通能力，高度注重数据准确性。
